text:
In Edmonton, Jason Dickinson is the checking centre the stars don't have to think about, and tonight he needs one assist for 100 in his career. He has four points in ten games, two of them goals, including a backhand rebound against Vancouver on Saturday.

The numbers around him are a strange pair. Edmonton has taken only 32% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, yet the Oilers have scored 4.7 more goals than those chances deserved. One of those numbers will move. Evolving-Hockey's read on his last season in Chicago helps explain it: he faced the other team's best (98th percentile competition) with weak teammates, and still took chances away, 86th percentile among forwards. His ice time is down almost three minutes a night over his last ten games. If the chance share doesn't improve, the luck won't cover for it forever, and a fourth-line role is where that usually ends.
